newsitem.title: UK: LVMH rules out buying Grand Metropolitan.
newsitem.headline: LVMH rules out buying Grand Metropolitan.

text.p: French luxury goods group LVMH said on Tuesday that it has no intention of making an offer for British drinks group Grand Metropolitan Plc.
LVMH said that it bought 4.75 million shares in Grand Metropolitan at an average price of 577 pence per share and now owns 0.23 percent of its share capital.
LVMH is in dispute with Guinness Plc, in which it holds a 14,2 percent stake, over the drinks group's proposed merger with GrandMet.

It requested an arbitration proceeding on Friday June 13 to settle the row with Guinness over whether it has the right to buy Guinness's stake in their joint distribution ventures and in champagne and spirits group Moet Hennessy, if Guinness goes ahead with the GrandMet merger.
LVMH argues that under the terms of agreements signed with Guinness a "control event" would enable LVMH to operate its joint ventures with Guinness independently.

LVMH voted against the proposed 24 billion pound ($39.3 billion) merger between Guinness and GrandMet, the largest in British corporate history, saying it would create a food and drinks giant with few synergies and fail to increase shareholder value.
